independent_reference.source: Yee-grid numerical-dispersion master relation (Schneider, Understanding the FDTD Method, dispersion chapter; spec section 3.7): [sin(w*dt/2)/(c*dt)]^2 = sum_xi [sin(k_xi*D/2)/D]^2, solved for |k| along theta by brentq; on-axis the 2D relation reduces to the 1D relation.

Second-order accuracy identity: the phase-velocity deficit 1 - vp/c scales as N_lambda^-2 (Yee scheme is O(Delta^2)); the 10-vs-20 cells-per-wavelength deficit ratio ~ 4 is asserted in packages/fdtd-optics/tests/test_golden_tables.py.

Second-order accuracy identity: the phase-velocity deficit 1 - vp/c scales as N_lambda^-2 (Yee scheme is O(Delta^2)); the 10-vs-20 cells-per-wavelength deficit ratio ~ 4 is asserted in packages/fdtd-optics/tests/test_golden_tables.py.

Independent published derivation of the same relation: Taflove & Hagness, Computational Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Ch. 4 (numerical dispersion and anisotropy) — error largest on-axis, smallest on the 45-deg diagonal, ordering asserted in packages/fdtd-optics/tests/test_golden_tables.py.
